meta.title: Nowon Lee — Frontend Engineer
meta.description: Technical profile of frontend engineer Nowon Lee, focused on information accuracy, document generation progress, interface responsiveness, and service reliability

identity.name: Nowon Lee
identity.lead: I analyze when and why problems occur in web services and design solutions that fit the requirements and existing systems.
identity.supporting: When large API responses caused the screen to freeze, I moved JSON parsing and data transformation to a Web Worker. For notes edited in multiple tabs, I designed the app to merge edits from each tab and preserve the input.

companies.summary: I developed the front end for the execution history detail view, server usage dashboard, and AI document generation service. I addressed freezes caused by large API responses and reduced the total data transferred by the server resource API. I designed a screen for reviewing drafts and generation details before download and coordinated the API response fields needed to display them.

contributions.title: Reducing rendering delays in the execution history detail view
paragraphs: Users reported that the screen froze when they opened certain execution records. I identified affected records from one week of execution history and used Chrome DevTools’ Network and Performance panels to inspect API request and response processing times. For responses of 300 MB or more, converting the responses into display values took time.

To reuse a worker across APIs, I considered passing a page-defined conversion function through Comlink or generating API-specific modules with code generation. The Comlink approach could run the conversion on the main thread. Generating a module for each API was unnecessary to resolve the freeze. I moved the detail view’s API request, JSON parsing, and display value conversion into a Web Worker and returned only the converted values to the page.

I saved a response that caused a freeze as a JSON file and ran three measurements before and three after introducing the Web Worker. The displayed values stayed the same, and rendering delay fell from about 360 ms to 50 ms or less.

contributions.title: Designing page modules around host routing and query caches
paragraphs: Our front end had to integrate as a library into a project that included another team’s service. The host team needed to control routing, and we could neither change its code nor provide a separate layout. I packaged the UI and behavior as page modules that the host could import without extra setup. The pages shared the host’s QueryClient when available and used a shared QueryClient from the package otherwise. This kept cached values and cache reset rules consistent across pages for the same query key.

After deployment, I found that styles defined outside CSS layers could override the package styles inside Tailwind CSS layers. I changed the package to load Tailwind’s theme, base styles, and utilities without assigning them to layers.

contributions.title: Improving Docker image request intake and parallel execution
paragraphs: The message service could not consume the next Kafka request until the running task finished. We considered committing the Kafka offset immediately after receiving a message. Keeping pending requests only in memory could lose them on restart, so I designed the intake sequence to store the request and its status in the database before committing the offset.

The service retrieved pending tasks from the database and assigned one task to each available Pod from a pre-created pool. I addressed issues encountered when building the task engine as a Docker image so the Pods could be prepared in advance. Pending tasks remained available after a restart, and multiple Pods could run tasks concurrently. I also designed chart tabs and tab selection in the execution history list so users could see resource usage for each Pod.

contributions.title: Showing document drafts and generation details before download
paragraphs: User feedback showed that reviewing an AI-generated document required downloading it first. I evaluated a library for rendering HWPX files. Integrating it posed risks for the project, and it could not show document generation details. Based on the feedback, I identified the response fields needed to show the document and its generation details, discussed them with the document generation API owner, and designed the screen and a Java proxy API.

Users could then view each section’s drafting status, the draft, and generation details before downloading. The detail page link and download button became available as soon as the completion event arrived, even while the detail status API response was still pending.

contributions.title: Reducing document generation status requests
paragraphs: With periodic polling, short intervals made extra calls to the detail API even when the status had not changed. Long intervals could delay the progress shown on screen. The existing SSE API sent events only when the generation stage changed. I designed the page to fetch details after each stage-change event and update the screen from the response. Detail API requests fell from 150–200 to 30 per document.

contributions.title: Reducing data transferred by the dashboard
paragraphs: I changed the dashboard to request only values newer than the previous request timestamp. Over 10 minutes, the amount of data transferred fell from 96.5 MB to 41 KB. I designed and implemented a Next.js API so the browser would no longer query Prometheus directly. I checked the values shown on the deployed dashboard against the API responses.

companies.summary: I made pages reflect user requests immediately, reduced the time it took for the first page to appear, and addressed issues that prevented real-time information from being shown. I documented the loading improvements so other projects could use the same approach.

contributions.title: Showing requested changes immediately and accurately
paragraphs: I made the page respond to user requests immediately, without waiting for a server response. I addressed mismatches between information on the page and server values, and reduced the request count by removing duplicate requests.

contributions.title: Shortening initial load and sharing a reusable setup
paragraphs: I reduced the time it took for pages to become visible to users. I documented the steps so other frontend projects could apply the same improvements.

contributions.title: Restoring real-time information updates
paragraphs: I used Chrome DevTools to find and fix intermittent WebSocket disconnections that stopped real-time information from updating.

contributions.summary: A URL could incorrectly match a route when it supplied an optional parameter without the preceding slash. I changed matching so patterns without a suffix could omit the optional parameter and its slash together. For patterns with a file extension, the parameter value can be omitted while the slash stays in place.
contributions.verification: I added tests for incorrectly matched URLs and existing file-extension patterns. The fix shipped in v7.13.1.

contributions.summary: Delete and Backspace could not remove the final character before an inline image in a regular paragraph or table cell. To preserve normal text and selection deletion, I applied a separate rule only when deleting a single remaining character immediately before an image with no text selected.
contributions.verification: The fix restored deletion of the final character before an image and shipped in v1.2.0.

items.title: AI Agent Workflow
paragraphs: I designed a review process that helps teammates identify what an AI-written document asks them to do and which part of the project it refers to. A script flags recurring informal phrases and wording whose meaning depends on context. The AI agent checks the project context before revising the sentence. For example, it replaced “document sharing boundaries” with an explanation of who can read a document under restricted sharing settings.

I designed a skill that checks existing requirements and code for the behavior to change and the conditions to preserve, so requests made in conversation are less likely to be missed or misread. When a choice affects who can use a feature or what it provides, the skill explains the difference and asks for confirmation. It continues unrelated research while waiting and records the agreed conditions and verification criteria. A document restructuring skill researches a structure suited to the document’s purpose, preserves the original wording while rearranging it, and leaves blanks where information is missing.

items.title: Personal Notes Workspace
paragraphs: I built a workspace for saving frequently used instructions and commands. Users can select content from several notes, arrange it, and copy it in one action. Editing a note in multiple tabs could leave only one tab’s changes. I considered asking users to choose a version, but that would interrupt editing and could discard edits they needed. I used Yjs Y.Text to merge insertions and deletions. To keep what tabs show consistent with what is stored, the app saves to IndexedDB before notifying other tabs through BroadcastChannel. Those tabs read the saved changes, and I designed an end-to-end test to check that edits from each tab appear.

I configured ESLint and JS Boundaries to check FSD layer imports and enforce separate server and browser entry points. I added arrow-key navigation to the batch-copy order menu using React Aria. Closing the menu returns focus to its trigger, and saving the order preserves focus in a note that is already being edited. I tested keyboard resizing and checked that bringing a note forward leaves the Tab order intact. I placed the IndexedDB provider at the app root, the batch-copy provider in the shared layout, and the editor provider on each editing page. Autosave tests can inject only what they need, and implementations can change without editing UI code.

items.title: Offline Translation Web App
paragraphs: With language models saved ahead of time, users can translate between Korean and English or Korean and Japanese without a network connection and keep entering text on the page while the model runs.
I used browser caching and IndexedDB to store the files and information needed for translation, and automated deployment with GitHub Actions.
